cats.name: Cash Cat
cats.catName: Cash Cat (the teary 'Crying Cat' from Vlad Tenev's 2021 meme)
cats.whoIsTheCat: Cash Cat was the working name Robinhood co-founders Vlad Tenev and Baiju Bhatt used before choosing 'Robinhood'. On 14 Apr 2021 Tenev confirmed it on X with a meme: a swole 'Robinhood' cat beside a teary 'cash cat'. That crying cat, a widely shared 'Crying Cat' edit (a meme format dating to 2014), became the token's face. The real cat in the photo is unidentified.

virality.summary: The name went viral in April 2021 when How I Built This posted that Robinhood's original name was 'Cash Cat' and Vlad Tenev quote-posted it with the swole-cat vs crying-cat meme. In 2026 the name was revived as the first breakout memecoin on Robinhood Chain; Bitstamp and then the Robinhood app itself (6 Aug 2026, also Robinhood Legend) listed it, the first Robinhood Chain memecoin offered to Robinhood's retail users.

Crying Cat page on Know Your Meme: 1,250,588 views (famous/raw/profiles_b0/knowyourmeme.com_memes_crying-cat.html). Robinhood app listing 2026-08-06 (AirdropAlert, Phemex).

coin.endorsedByOwner: No. The project site says it is not affiliated with Robinhood Markets, Inc. or Vlad Tenev ('fan fiction with a ticker'). Robinhood sells CASHCAT in its app since 6 Aug 2026, which is a listing decision, not an endorsement (Phemex).

cats.lore: Before there was a Robinhood, there was almost a Cash Cat. It was the working name Vlad Tenev and Baiju Bhatt used before they picked the folk hero, and in April 2021 Tenev confirmed it with a meme: a swole Robinhood cat next to a small, teary Cash Cat. When Robinhood Chain opened in summer 2026, anonymous fans gave the forgotten name a home on-chain, with that crying cat as its face. Its own site calls it fan fiction with a ticker and says the cat lives on Robinhood Chain now because the vibes feel familiar.

cats.name: Catecoin
cats.catName: Atsuko Sato's rescued kitten (reported as 'Momo'; name unconfirmed)
cats.whoIsTheCat: A tiny rescued kitten that Atsuko Sato, owner of Kabosu (the Shiba Inu behind Doge), shared in a short video on 26 Jul 2026. MarsBit/CoinW call the kitten Momo; a July 2026 Osso Magazine interview names Sato's newest rescue Rika-chan, so the name is unconfirmed. Sato says her post was used without permission and she has no ties to CATE. The logo is an illustrated tabby kitten.

virality.summary: Hours after Kabosu's owner shared a kitten clip on 26 Jul 2026, traders launched CATE on pump.fun as 'the cat sister of Dogecoin' (Dog+E, Cat+E); it rose about 230x on day one. On 28 Jul Sato said the CATE tokens have no connection to her. The original deployer later left and the trader PoorGoat took over (community takeover). Gate listed CATE spot on 30 Aug and later perpetuals.
virality.metrics: ~230x in a single day, peak ~$9.5M mcap on launch day per GMGN (Bitcoinworld via Bitget/cryptonews, 27 Jul 2026). Over 124,000 holders on 18 Sep (BTCC citing CoinMarketCap); 137.2K holders on 25 Sep (catearmy.com). BubbleMaps: 25 wallets held ~19% of supply (3 Aug). The original kitten post was not located; per Sato it was an Instagram story, which expires, and view counts are not available.

coin.endorsedByOwner: No. On 28 Jul 2026 Atsuko Sato said the CATE tokens have no connection to her and that her post (an Instagram story, per Sato) was used without authorization; her only authorized IP partner is Own The Doge (DOG, COCORO) (Cointime via Bitget News; BSCN; MarsBit/CoinW).

cats.lore: In July 2026 Atsuko Sato, whose photos of Kabosu became Doge, shared a short clip of a tiny rescued kitten. Within hours, strangers on Solana launched CATE, 'the cat sister of Dogecoin': Dog plus E, Cat plus E. Its first dev drifted away and the community carried it on. Sato has said she has no connection to CATE and did not agree to her post being used. So here the kitten stays what it really is: a small rescue with eyes closed and chin up, and a reminder that the best cat stories start with someone taking a cat home.

cats.name: Purr
cats.whoIsTheCat: Hypurr is Hyperliquid's cartoon cat: a white kitten with gray tabby stripes in a black hoodie, who posts on X as @Hyperintern, the exchange's 'chief intern officer'. It is the face of PURR, the first token on Hyperliquid's spot market (16 Apr 2024), and of the 4,600-piece Hypurr NFT collection airdropped on 28 Sep 2025. A drawn character; there is no real cat behind it.

virality.summary: PURR went live on 16 Apr 2024 as the first HIP-1 token on Hyperliquid, airdropped to points holders with no sale and no team allocation, and became the ecosystem's community memecoin. The cat reached a wider audience in Sep 2025 when Hyperliquid airdropped 4,600 Hypurr NFTs to Genesis participants; floors opened around $60k to $69k and one Hypurr (#21) sold for about $467k.
virality.metrics: @HyperliquidX launch post (2024-04-16 05:00 UTC): 874 likes, 96 replies, read today from X's public syndication endpoint (famous/raw/profiles_b0/x_synd_1780098887015072013.json). Hypurr NFT drop: 4,600 NFTs, 4,300+ to Genesis participants, OTC floor $65k-$100k in the first hours, #21 sold for nearly $500k (AirdropAlert, 29 Sep 2025); The Block and others reported about $45M traded on day one (search snippets; pages blocked here).

cats.lore: Before Hyperliquid had its own token, it had a cat. On 16 April 2024 PURR became the very first token on Hyperliquid's native spot market, handed out to early users with no sale and no team allocation, a test that simply stuck around. Its face is Hypurr, a white kitten with gray tabby stripes and a black hoodie who posts as the exchange's chief intern officer. In 2025 the same cat family came back as the Hypurr NFT collection, gifted to Hyperliquid's earliest users. PURR itself has no utility, just a very loyal cat.

cats.name: Anonymous Cat
cats.catName: Anonymous Cat (an unidentified white cat in a paper bag)
cats.whoIsTheCat: An unidentified white cat photographed with a brown paper bag over its head: two round eye holes, a nose hole, and a dark collar with a round silver tag. The photo is the logo of Anonymous Cat, a memecoin themed on Zcash's privacy, launched on StonkFun (Solana) on 30 Aug 2026. No source names the cat, its owner or the photographer, and the project has no team or socials.

virality.summary: Launched quietly on StonkFun on 30 Aug 2026 and paired against ZEC instead of SOL, ZCAT took off in the first week of September as Zcash rallied. Every transfer carries a 3% tax that is converted to ZEC and airdropped to holders. CoinDesk covered it on 7 Sep 2026, CoinGecko said cat-themed tokens passed $1B total market cap during the ZCAT rally, and influencers such as Ansem posted their ZEC rewards.
virality.metrics: By 7 Sep 2026 the project dashboard showed about 2,320 ZEC (~$2.8M) paid out across more than 470,000 payouts (CoinDesk). Ranked #5 of 15 on CoinGecko trending at 06:40 UTC on 7 Sep (Phemex). 18,596 holders on 7 Sep (GeckoTerminal via Phemex). No original viral post: the cat photo's source is unknown.

cats.lore: Some cats want to be seen. This one prefers a paper bag. Anonymous Cat showed up on StonkFun at the end of August 2026: a white cat peeking through two neat eye holes, pink nose poking out below, a small salute to Zcash's love of privacy. No team, no socials, no face; the bag is the whole brand. Every ZCAT transfer pays a 3% tax that is turned into ZEC and sent to holders' wallets. Nobody knows who the cat under the bag is, and that is exactly the point.
